headline: Blue Origin is reported to move New Glenn's return to flight into January 2027 as NASA's Swift observatory is reported to have fallen to Earth.
summary: The Financial Times, relayed by Reuters, and Bloomberg reported on 5 November that Blue Origin has moved New Glenn's return to flight into January 2027, and no company page in the packet confirms it.
Frankfurter Allgemeine reported on 5 November that NASA's Swift observatory fell to Earth, a single-source claim with no NASA page behind it.
Bloomberg reported on 5 November that SpaceX's default-risk measure reached a record high, which is a market gauge and not a default.
OHB said on an undated newsroom page that it has been awarded a EUR 554 million Sentinel-3 Next Generation Topography contract, a company claim with no ESA or EU page alongside.
Breaking Defense reported on 5 November that Ukraine is eyeing a new Starshield deal by mid-2027, a stated hope and not a signed contract.
bottom_line: The facts move New Glenn from a flight with no confirmed slip to a return to flight reported for January, and they close the Swift thread pending a NASA page. They do not move the dated European decisions, the 10 November committee vote and the 15 December Rome meeting.

global.exposure: US heavy-lift launch schedule and the Blue Origin cadence request before the FAA
global.title: Blue Origin is reported to move New Glenn's return to flight into January 2027 as the 30 October FAA comment deadline passes with no decision on file
global.summary: The Financial Times, relayed by Reuters on 5 November, reported that Blue Origin has delayed New Glenn's return to flight into January, and the report cites no company statement in the packet. Bloomberg reported the same delay on 5 November, and the Seattle Times, Quartz and U.S. News carried reports of it the same day, which counts as two independent chains and not six. Quartz put the return to flight in January 2027, but the packet holds headlines only and no day within the month. Blue Origin had asked the FAA on an earlier date to allow up to 50 New Glenn launches a year from Florida, and the 30 October comment deadline has passed with no FAA decision in the packet. No Blue Origin page in the packet confirms the delay, so the slip is reported and not announced.
global.why: A January return would leave New Glenn without a flight for the rest of 2026 on the reported schedule. The FAA cadence request is a separate matter that the delay does not settle.
global.bar: Two independent sources (Financial Times via Reuters, Bloomberg); no government page and no national-language source.

global.exposure: NASA astrophysics assets and orbital debris handling
global.title: NASA's Swift observatory is reported to have fallen to Earth, closing a thread opened by the end of science operations on 23 October
global.summary: Only one source in the packet, Frankfurter Allgemeine, reported on 5 November that the Swift space telescope has crashed back to Earth. Its headline places the fall after a rescue mission, and the packet gives no time, place or detail of the re-entry. NASA ended Swift's science operations on 23 October, and the 26 October edition already carried the abandoned reboost. No NASA page in the packet confirms the re-entry, so the date and location remain unconfirmed. The thread is closed pending any NASA statement, and no replacement plan or reversal of the shutdown appears in the packet.
global.why: The dated event the thread was waiting for has arrived, on one German-language report. No replacement mission is named in the packet.
global.bar: One source; no government page and no national-language source for the country concerned.

global.exposure: Financing conditions for the largest US launch provider
global.title: Bloomberg reports SpaceX's default risk at a record high in a tech-led credit slump, a market reading and not a company event
global.summary: Only one source in the packet, Bloomberg, reported on 5 November that SpaceX's default risk hit a record high. The headline ties the move to a broader tech-driven credit slump and does not give a figure in the packet. No SpaceX statement appears in the packet. A default-risk reading is a market gauge, not a default, a downgrade or a change to launch plans. The packet does not show how the measure is built or who is quoting it.
global.why: The reading shows how credit markets priced SpaceX on 5 November. It does not change any launch, contract or customer commitment on file.
global.bar: One source; no government page and no national-language source.

items.exposure: European lunar infrastructure studies ahead of the Rome meeting

audio_sections.title: Opening
audio_sections.text: This is Sovereign Space ATLAS for 5 November 2026. This edition carries three global items and at least one item from each regional desk. The lead is a reported delay to the return of New Glenn. Each claim is limited to what its sources say, and single-source claims are marked.

audio_sections.title: Top story
audio_sections.text: Blue Origin is reported to have moved the return to flight of New Glenn into January 2027. The Financial Times reported the delay, and Reuters relayed it on 5 November. Bloomberg reported it separately the same day. Other outlets repeated those reports. No Blue Origin page in the reading packet confirms the delay. The company has asked the FAA to allow up to 50 launches a year from Florida. Comments on that request were due on 30 October, and no FAA decision is on file. Blue Origin also announced a third stage for New Glenn and a new booster engine called Northstar on 5 November. That announcement came with no flight date.

audio_sections.title: Around the world
audio_sections.text: NASA's Swift observatory has fallen to Earth, according to the German newspaper Frankfurter Allgemeine on 5 November. That is the only source in the packet. It describes the fall as following a rescue mission. The packet does not give the time or place, and no NASA page confirms it. Swift ended science operations on 23 October, and an earlier reboost was abandoned. Separately, Bloomberg reported on 5 November that SpaceX's default risk reached a record high in a tech-led credit slump. That is one source, and it reports a market gauge, not a default. The packet carries no SpaceX statement.

audio_sections.title: Europe
audio_sections.text: OHB says on its own newsroom that it has been awarded a EUR 554 million contract for the Copernicus Sentinel-3 Next Generation Topography satellite. The page is undated in the packet, and no ESA or EU page confirms it. OHB also says ESA has awarded it OASIS studies towards a European lunar infrastructure. That too is a company claim. ArianeGroup dated a second successful SyLEx sounding rocket launch to 4 November. Its earlier page says Arianespace will launch 36 Amazon Leo satellites on the tenth Ariane 6 flight on 23 November at the earliest. No ESA or EU decision arrived in the packet. The next are the European Parliament industry committee vote on the EU Space Act on 10 November and the ESA meeting in Rome on 15 December.

audio_sections.title: Closer to home
audio_sections.text: Breaking Defense reported on 5 November that Ukraine is eyeing a new SpaceX Starshield deal by mid-2027. The report says there are still no answers about problems in October. It is one source, and mid-2027 is a hope, not a contract. In the Nordics, no item in the packet met the source rule. In Eurasia, Meduza reported a researcher's finding that Russian space startups may be passing off Chinese satellite imagery as their own. That is an allegation from one source. In the Middle East, Anadolu reports a US intelligence report describing Iran as an emerging space power. The report itself is not in the packet. In Asia Pacific, the South China Morning Post reports atoms chilled to a record low on the Tiangong station. Der Spiegel reports on 3 November that China plans a crewed Moon landing before 2030. Neither report carries a Chinese government page.

audio_sections.title: Industry and markets
audio_sections.text: NASASpaceflight reported on 1 November that Isaacman outlined an Artemis III multi-launch checkout sequence and a Blue Origin priority. That is one source, headline only. NASA's stated dates are unchanged in the packet: a landing in 2028, and commercial station proposals due 8 December. Payload reported that Redwire won a 20 million dollar DARPA contract for a second very low Earth orbit demonstration. Payload also reported that Northwood Space raised 375 million dollars in a Series C at a 2 billion dollar valuation. It reported that Tumbleweed raised 6.9 million euros to build its own reentry vehicle. And it reported that Starfish lost contact with its Otter spacecraft, cutting its mission short. Each is a single press report.

audio_sections.title: The days ahead
audio_sections.text: The next dated event is 10 November, the European Parliament industry committee vote on the EU Space Act. The Ariane 6 flight with 36 Amazon Leo satellites is set for 23 November at the earliest. NASA commercial space-station proposals are due on 8 December. The ESA intermediate ministerial meeting takes place in Rome on 15 December. Blue Origin's reported January return to flight has no date.

audio_sections.title: Close
audio_sections.text: That was the 5 November edition of Sovereign Space ATLAS. The facts changed today are a reported New Glenn slip, the fall of Swift, and company-reported European contracts. None of them settles a decision.
